title: Context Menu UX Engineering
summary: This lesson covers the technical and design details of context menus, including collision detection, grouping by intent, and the 'safe triangle' for submenus. It also highlights keyboard accessibility and cross-platform consistency between desktop and mobile.

transcript.text: Right-click near the edge. Watch the menu flip. It measured first.
A context menu measures before it opens. No room below, it flips up. No room right, it mirrors left.
Anchored to your cursor, always inside the viewport.
12 flat actions read as noise. Group by intent, split with dividers.
Rename with duplicate, share with copy link, and delete alone at the bottom, in red.
Submenus die when the cursor drifts. So Figma draws an invisible triangle from cursor to submenu.
Inside that path, the menu holds. That's hover intent.
Power users never aim. Arrows walk the list, letters jump.
Press D, land on duplicate. Escape closes one level, not the whole thing.
Mobile has no right-click. A long press opens the same actions as a bottom sheet.
Context menus are a system. Follow for more UX engineering. Save this for your next build.

before_after: A list of 12 flat actions is transformed into a structured menu grouped by intent with dividers and a highlighted destructive action.
